battle.name: 交趾之戰
battle.theater: 安南都護府交趾龍編城
battle.brief: 大中八年（854），南詔王世隆遣將自雲南沿紅河南下，攻陷唐朝安南都護府治所龍編城，該州自此淪入南詔統治。唐軍把弩手列於城垣與壘柵之後，居高拒南詔象兵與步卒；秦弩正是守方的主要遠射兵器，一張一發，壓住攻城者接近牆根的節奏。城破之後唐廷未能即時收復，直到咸通年間高驪收復愛州、驩州。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 854 年春天到夏初，交戰的兩方是唐王朝與南詔國。唐朝在交趾的統治機構是安南都護府，即交趾郡，治所在龍編城，位置在今越南北部紅河下游三角洲，漢代以來便是中原王朝設郡置縣最南的落腳點。唐廷以安南都護為正副主官，節制交趾的兵馬與城防，軍令由兵部、尚書省一道行文；兵源一部分是京師宿衛與嶺南、桂管、容管等道調發的蕃兵與團練，一部分就地徵集。交趾一處的常駐兵額與實際可用之兵向來有差，糧餉則靠嶺南諸州自廣州轉輸，或循海道自揚州、福州出海而至。南詔此時是洱海地區的南詔國，都城在太和城，即今大理一帶，在位之王為世隆，823 年至 859 年在位；世隆以武力爭得王位之後，段氏等大族分掌兵權，南詔軍隊以「軍」與「部」編制，兵種兼有步卒、騎兵與象兵，兵源為洱海各部落的丁壯與歷年戰俘，另有安南、嶺北方向的附屬部眾。紅河是兩國的分界：北岸一線是唐的交趾，南面是南詔的雲南高原，東邊則是占城、真臘等小國。南詔要的是紅河三角洲的稻米、海道與嶺南商路，唐朝守交趾，是把它當作西南的屏蔽與通往南海的門戶。
countriesEn: In the spring and early summer of 854 the two belligerents were the Tang dynasty and the kingdom of Nanzhao. Tang administered Jiaozhi through the Annan Protectorate, that is, the commandery of Jiaozhi, whose seat was Longbian, in the delta of the Red River in what is now northern Vietnam, and since the Han the southernmost fixed point of a Chinese administrative district. The court appointed a chief and a deputy protector at Annan to control the garrison and the defences of Jiaozhi, and the orders travelled down through the Ministry of War and the Department of State Affairs. The troops came partly from the imperial guard and from the tribal levies and the militia of the Lingnan, Guiguan and Rongguan circuits, and were partly levied on the spot. The nominal garrison at Jiaozhi was regularly larger than the men actually under arms, and its grain came from the Lingnan prefectures by way of Guangzhou, or by sea from Yangzhou and Fuzhou. Nanzhao at that time was the kingdom of the Erhai region, with its capital at Taihe, near modern Dali, ruled by King Shilong, who held the throne from 823 to 859. Shilong had won the throne by force, and great families such as the Duan shared the command of the army afterwards. The Nanzhao host was organised into armies and divisions combining foot, horse and elephants, drawn from the able-bodied men of the Erhai tribes and from war captives taken over the years, together with subordinate groups from Annam and from the northern marches. The Red River was the frontier: the northern bank line was Tang's Jiaozhi, the south was the Yunnan plateau of Nanzhao, and to the east lay the smaller states of Champa and Chenla. What Nanzhao wanted was the rice of the delta, the sea route and the trade of Lingnan; what Tang wanted to keep at Jiaozhi was a screen against the south-west and the gateway to the southern seas.
people: 留下姓名的，交戰一方在唐，另一方在南詔。唐宣宗李忱在位（846 至 859），大中年間正是朝廷想收拾西南的時候；朝中宰臣與邊鎮主張互有出入，同朋黨爭一線在藩鎮、財政與邊防之間拉扯，許多決策因此拖延。交趾方面的主將蔡袭在兵難中戰死，《新唐書·南蠻傳》與《資治通鑑》都記他以身殉職，但對他死難所屬的年份，各家繫法不一，或繫於大中八年南詔首度攻陷交趾之役，或繫於咸通年間南詔再攻交趾之役。南詔方面，國王世隆在位時把兵權交給段氏等大族，段宗牂（史籍亦作段宗）是《新唐書·南蠻傳》中最常與南詔攻交趾連繫在一起的名字，他領的是雲南方面的主力。咸通年間，唐廷先後以交趾招討使的名號遣將赴安南，仍未能扭轉局勢；其後高驪出任安南都護，在咸通年間收復愛州與驩州，才把交趾重新置回唐朝的版圖。高驪是幽州人，出身北方軍門，臨安南之前已在嶺南與西南一線領兵多年，所以《舊唐書》與《新唐書》都把唐廷在交趾的最後一搏記在他名下。地方基層的姓名多已不傳，留在《蠻書》與《南蠻傳》中的多是某一段、某人一事的零星記載，兵與糧的細帳則幾乎全部散失。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive stand on either side. Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Li Chen, reigned from 846 to 859, and the Dazhong years were a time when the court meant to settle the south-west; the ministers at the centre and the commanders in the circuits disagreed, and the line of the factional rivalry between the Niu and Li pulled at them across the questions of the provincial commands, the finances and the frontier, so that many decisions were delayed. On the Jiaozhi side the commander Cai Xi was killed in the fighting; both the Account of the Southern Barbarians in the New History of Tang and the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid to Government record that he died in the breach, but the histories differ on the year, some placing his death in the campaign of 854 in which Nanzhao first took Jiaozhi, others in the renewed attack of the Xiantong years. On the Nanzhao side, King Shilong handed the conduct of war to great families such as the Duan after his accession, and the name most often linked in the New History of Tang with the Nanzhao attack on Jiaozhi is Duan Zongzhuang, also written Duan Zong, who led the main body out of Yunnan. In the Xiantong years the Tang court sent commanders to Annan again and again under the title of commander for Jiaozhi, and still could not reverse the situation. Gao Pian then took up the post of protector of Annan and recovered Aizhou and Xuanzhou during the Xiantong years, and only then was Jiaozhi set back inside the Tang map. Gao Pian was a man of Youzhou, born into a military family of the north, and he had led troops on the Lingnan and south-western lines for years before he came to Annan, which is why both the Old History of Tang and the New History of Tang place the last Tang effort in Jiaozhi under his name. The names of the local officers have largely been lost; what survives in the Manshu and the Account of the Southern Barbarians is fragmentary, in the form of a certain district or a certain man, while the detailed accounts of the men and of the grain are almost entirely gone.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩，是漢代到唐代一直壓在城頭與陣前的那件兵器：弓靠射手臂力，弩靠機關蓄力，射手把弦上滿、置於弩機之上，扣機而發，一矢一發，射程遠過弓，精度也高，無遮蔽的遠目標可以取準；弩的代價在於上弦費時，所以步卒之中往往弩手與裝填手配合，或排成橫陣，發一輪即退步重上。唐軍的弩分腰張與臂張兩路，腰張弩要用足踏上弦牀，張好之後再取下上機；安南都護府與嶺南諸鎮的守城序列裡，弩手分層布於城頭、壘柵之後與城門缺口，居高向下封住攻城的接近路線，這正是唐家在交趾最倚重的一道火線。南詔軍中同樣有弓有弩，但真正的殺傷骨幹是象兵：披甲的巨象背上築有塔位，載兵居高射弩、撒標槍，步卒在象側以大盾與藤牌護身，用南詔直刃刀近身；攻城時配雲梯、撞車、巢車一類器械，唐軍在火藥箭與「猛火油」塗刷器械的用法之外，主要仍靠弩、砲石與城體本身的堅固。運輸一端，南詔靠象力與舟船自雲南沿紅河而下，並以牛馬負糧；唐軍的糧餉由廣州經海道與嶺南陸路北運，弩箭、弓弦、槊桿這類耗物才真正卡在這條線上。
kitsEn: The Qin crossbow on the card is the weapon that Chinese armies from the Han down to the Tang kept on the wall and at the head of the line. A bow depends on the strength of the shooter's arm; a crossbow depends on a mechanism that stores the pull. The archer sets the string, lays the bolt on the trigger assembly and releases it: one bolt at a time, with a range well beyond that of a bow and an accuracy good enough to take an unobstructed distant mark. The price of the crossbow is the time needed to reload, so in a foot formation the crossbowmen worked with men who loaded for them, or stood in a line and fired a volley before stepping back to reload. The crossbows of the Tang army were of the waist-drawing and arm-drawing kinds, the waist-drawing type being cocked with the foot on a drawing frame and then lifted onto the trigger. In the defence sequences of the Annan Protectorate and of the Lingnan commands, the crossbowmen were posted in tiers on the wall, behind the stockade and at the gaps in the gate, shooting downward to seal the approach of the attackers; this was the line of fire on which the Tang in Jiaozhi relied most. Nanzhao had bows and crossbows too, but the real weight of its killing lay with the elephants: armoured animals carried a platform on their backs with soldiers standing on it to shoot crossbows and throw javelins, while the infantry at their flank covered themselves with large shields and rattan shields and closed with the long Nanzhao sabre. The siege train brought scaling ladders, battering rams and watch towers. The Tang, beyond the use of fire arrows and of machines smeared with fierce fire oil, still relied chiefly on crossbows, stone shot and the solidity of the walls themselves. On the line of supply, Nanzhao moved its food on elephants and boats down the Red River from Yunnan, with oxen and horses carrying the rest, while Tang grain came north from Guangzhou by sea and by the overland road of Lingnan; and it was the expendable things, bolts, bowstrings and spear shafts, that truly jammed that line.
tactics: 南詔出兵的走法，先在雲南集兵，再分兩路：一路順紅河谷地順流而下，舟船與象隊夾道而進；一路取嶺南山道，步騎並行。兩路的目標都是交趾城，兵力的核心是象兵與隨象而來的步兵。攻城之前，南詔先以弩箭與標槍覆蓋城外，把唐軍的巡邏與反衝壓在城壕之內，再使象群與步卒分批逼近，試探唐軍的火力與城門的消耗；唐軍的應法是收縮城外的壘柵，把弩手集中到城頭與城門兩側，憑居高之勢逐次射擊象背與象奴，試圖使象驚退，並在城門外壘木柵、置拒馬以延緩衝撞的時間。問題在於弩的射界受城垣與壘柵所限，一旦南詔兵卒貼到牆根，弩箭的角度就難以施展，而城下的象仍可直接撞擊土牆。唐軍的後勤是另一層束縛：交趾距京師數千里，糧秣要自嶺南或海道接運，雨季一到，泥濘與瘧癘會同時拖累行軍與守軍的體力；守軍的士氣與兵額本來就不足，一場耗時的圍城足以把它拖垮。最終城防崩潰，守軍在城內巷戰失利，主將死於兵難，交趾遂落入南詔之手。
tacticsEn: The way Nanzhao marched went like this. The army was mustered first in Yunnan and then went out in two columns: one down the valley of the Red River with the current, boats and elephant trains moving together; the other by the mountain road of Lingnan, foot and horse in company. The object of both was the city of Jiaozhi, and the core of the force was the elephants with the infantry who came with them. Before the assault Nanzhao covered the ground outside the walls with crossbow bolts and javelins, holding Tang patrols and counter-charges inside the ditch, and only then sent the elephants and the foot forward in successive batches to test the Tang fire and to wear at the gates. Tang answered by pulling its stockades in, concentrating the crossbowmen on the wall and on both flanks of the gate, shooting in turn at the elephants' backs and their drivers in the hope of scaring the animals off, and blocking the gate with timber and chevaux-de-frise to buy time against the shock. The difficulty was that the field of fire of the crossbow was confined by the wall and the stockade: once the Nanzhao foot was at the foot of the rampart the bolts could hardly be laid, and the elephants could still strike the earth wall directly. Tang supply was another knot. Jiaozhi lay thousands of li from the capital, its grain had to come by the roads of Lingnan or by sea, and once the rains came, mud and fever laid hold on marching troops and garrison alike. The garrison was short of men and short of spirit to begin with, and one siege long enough in the telling was enough to wear it out. In the end the defences gave way, the defenders were beaten in the streets of the city, the commander died in the breach, and Jiaozhi passed into the hands of Nanzhao.
data: 可核的數字不多，幾項硬的是這樣的。年份是唐宣宗大中八年，即 854 年；南詔王世隆在位 823 至 859 年，段氏掌兵的年代與此相合。地名上，交趾治所在龍編城，即今越南河內一帶，紅河在此入海；往南是愛州（今清化一帶），再往西北折是驩州（今諒山、永福一帶），這三處是交趾與雲南之間的南北骨幹。唐軍若要自嶺南反攻交趾，走的是廣州與桂管（今廣西桂林一線）向西南的陸路，或自海上自廣州溯流西上。戰役時間，若以唐廷命將、兵部發糧到城破為序，約在數月之內；之後唐朝收復交趾的過程卻拖了十餘年，直到咸通年間高驪收復愛州、驩州才告一段落。兵力的直接記載幾乎空白，只能從前後兩役推知量級：天寶年間唐廷曾以號稱十萬的眾深入交趾而全軍覆沒，咸通末年高驪出師時所統也是以萬計的兵力與象兵；南詔方面的兵眾在各史書中多以「眾」字帶過，沒有可用的確數。損失與掠奪，史料只說南詔攻陷交趾後取去糧秣與器物，數目「無算」，不宜換算成具體人數。器械方面可確定的只有弩的射速特性：弩手發一矢之後必須重新上弦，因此同一部隊的實際射擊是分批輪射，而不是連續齊射，故一支弩隊在城頭能覆蓋的正面寬度，也就受制於裝填的速度。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and a few of them are hard. The year was the eighth of the Dazhong era of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, that is 854; King Shilong of Nanzhao reigned from 823 to 859, and the dating of the Duan family's command of the army fits. As to places: the seat of Jiaozhi was Longbian, in what is now the Hanoi area of Vietnam, where the Red River reaches the sea; to the south lay Aizhou, around modern Thanh Hoa, and turning back to the north-west, Xuanzhou, around modern Hoa Binh and Luong Son. Those three places were the backbone of the north-south line between Jiaozhi and Yunnan. A Tang army marching back from Lingnan to retake Jiaozhi would come by the road from Guangzhou and the Guiguan circuit, in the modern Guangxi line around Guilin, or by sea from Guangzhou up the river. As to the duration of the campaign, from the court sending a commander and the Ministry of War issuing grain to the fall of the city was a matter of some months; but the process of recovering Jiaozhi afterwards dragged on for more than a decade, until Gao Pian took back Aizhou and Xuanzhou in the Xiantong years. There is almost no direct record of the numbers engaged, so only the order of magnitude can be inferred from the campaigns on either side. In the Tianbao years the Tang sent a host said to number a hundred thousand into Jiaozhi and it was annihilated; when Gao Pian took the field in the later Xiantong years he too commanded a force counted in tens of thousands together with his elephants. Nanzhao's numbers are given in the histories mostly in the vague form of a host, with no figure that can be used. Losses and plunder are likewise given only in general terms: the sources say that after taking Jiaozhi the Nanzhao carried off grain and equipment beyond counting, and that should not be turned into a specific number of men. On equipment, the only point that can be settled is the rate of fire of the crossbow: after a bolt was loosed the archer had to re-cock, so the shooting of any one unit went in successive volleys rather than as a continuous barrage, and the width of frontage that a single band of crossbowmen could cover from the wall was therefore governed by the speed of loading.
cause: 打起來的緣由有三層。最外面一層是地理與資源：紅河三角洲的稻米足以支撐一支大軍，海道又通往廣州與占城，南詔若要把勢力從雲南高原推到紅河下游，就必須取走交趾；而唐廷把交趾看作屏蔽南詔、控住南海商路的門戶，不可能讓出。第二層是世隆朝南詔內部的權力局面：世隆以兵權得位，段氏等大族掌軍，國策由強臣與擴張的胃口推著走，雲南本地的土地與資源已經分得差不多，向交趾用兵既是擴張，也是分贓。中間夾着一層更舊的舊帳：從天寶年間閣羅鳳與唐交戰、鮮于仲通與李宓先後領兵深入而全軍覆沒，到其後數十年唐與南詔在邊界上反覆爭奪，雙方對交趾的歸屬從來沒有真正談妥過；唐廷每次都當交趾是南詔的藩屬，視之為西南屏障，南詔則把唐廷的出兵視為逼迫。最裡面一層是唐廷自己的虛弱：交趾的兵額長期不足，糧餉靠嶺南接運，中樞與邊鎮互相推諉，兵部的行文到交趾往往要輾轉數月才有回音；宣宗一朝想把西南收拾好，卻先要處理藩鎮與財政，再遇上朋黨之爭，兵與糧就都成了空話。
causeEn: There were three layers behind the fighting. The outermost was geography and resources. The rice of the Red River delta could feed a large army, and the sea route led on to Guangzhou and to Champa; if Nanzhao meant to push its power from the Yunnan plateau down to the lower Red River, it had to take Jiaozhi. Tang, for its part, held Jiaozhi as a screen against Nanzhao and as the door onto the southern trade, and could not give it up. The second layer was the internal balance of power in Nanzhao under Shilong: he had taken the throne by military force, great families such as the Duan held the army, and policy was driven on by strong ministers and by the appetite for expansion, with the land and resources of Yunnan itself already divided as far as they would go. Attacking Jiaozhi was therefore both expansion and a share-out. The next layer inward was an older account. From the fighting between Nanzhao and Tang under Gebiaofeng in the Tianbao years, through the annihilation of the armies led by Xianyu Zhongtong and then by Li Mi, to the repeated disputes over the frontier in the decades that followed, the ownership of Jiaozhi had never truly been settled. The Tang court each time treated Jiaozhi as a vassal state of Nanzhao and as the shield of the south-west, while Nanzhao treated the Tang expeditions as oppression. The innermost layer was the weakness of the Tang court itself. The garrison at Jiaozhi was chronically short of men, the grain came by a long road from Lingnan, the central secretariat and the frontier command shifted responsibility onto one another, and an order from the Ministry of War often took months of circuit before it drew any reply at all. The Xuanzong reign wished to put the south-west in order, but had first to deal with the provincial commands and the finances, and then with the factional rivalry; soldiers and grain alike ended up as talk.
impact: 這場仗的直接後果，是唐朝在紅河下游的統治中斷。安南都護府這個建置空了十餘年：交趾自 854 年落入南詔，直到咸通年間高驪收復愛州、驩州，唐朝的旗號才重新立回紅河之濱；其後又設安南節度使，把軍政與民政合在一處，以免再出現守將各自為政、兵無所屬的局面。對南詔而言，這是世隆朝疆域最闊的時期，越南北部與雲南連成一片，南詔的物產與商人從此可以直下海路，雲南的銅、鹽、馬匹與交趾的稻米、漁獲在同一条商道上流動；南詔與唐的關係也就此從「藩屬—宗主」轉為對等的爭奪，直到 902 年前後南詔內亂、其後高氏建大長和、段氏建大理，雲南的政治格局為之一變。對兵器與戰術的意義同樣不小：唐廷在這十餘年裡被迫重新計算西南的用兵，弩、砲石與火藥箭在攻守之間的配比、城防的形制、糧道由海轉陸的問題，都被一次又一次重新試算；而南詔的象兵在這十餘年裡一直是壓在唐軍城頭上的那根槓桿，直到高驪以火藥箭焚燒南詔的竹木城與器械，才第一次在裝備上佔到上風。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the battle was an interruption of Tang rule in the lower Red River. The institution of the Annan Protectorate stood empty for more than a decade: from 854 Jiaozhi belonged to Nanzhao, and it was not until the Xiantong years, when Gao Pian recovered Aizhou and Xuanzhou, that Tang authority was planted again on the banks of the Red River. The court then set up the military governorship of Annan, combining the military and the civil administration in one, so that no separate commanders should again leave the garrison with no master. For Nanzhao it was the widest the kingdom's territory ever ran in Shilong's reign: northern Vietnam and Yunnan became one block, Nanzhao's produce and merchants could go straight down to the sea, and the copper, salt and horses of Yunnan and the rice and fish of Jiaozhi moved along the same road. The relation between Nanzhao and Tang turned in consequence from that of vassal and overlord into a contest between equals, and stayed that way until the disorder in Nanzhao around 902 and the later foundation of the Dali kingdom by the Gao and Duan families changed the political map of Yunnan. The lesson in arms and in warfare was no smaller. For more than a decade the Tang court was forced to calculate its south-western war afresh: the balance of crossbows, stone shot and fire arrows in attack and defence, the shape of the fortifications, the question of shifting the supply line from sea to land, each was worked out again and again. And the elephants of Nanzhao remained the lever pressing on the Tang walls the whole time, until Gao Pian burned the bamboo-and-timber works and siege machines of Nanzhao with fire arrows and gained the upper hand in equipment for the first time.
result: 結果是南詔得手，唐朝失守。交趾城破之後，守軍潰散，主將死於兵難，唐廷的安南都護府名存實亡，嶺南與雲南之間再沒有屏障；南詔得以把勢力線推到紅河下游，取得稻米、海道與商稅，大軍屯駐在城郊，等待下一次攻擊的時機。往後十餘年，唐與南詔在交趾方向的反覆拉鋸，始終沒有解決問題：咸通年間朝廷先後派遣交趾招討使，兵部屢次發糧，卻因兵員不齊、糧運不繼、將領互不相屬而一再錯過戰機，直到高驪以安南都護之任收復愛州、驩州，才把南詔的攻勢壓回紅河以北。就這場戰爭本身而言，可以確定的是：南詔以象兵與步兵攻破了唐朝在交趾的城防，交趾隨之易主，而唐廷的弩手曾在城頭把攻城者壓在牆外許久，卻終究未能守住這座城；唐人對這段失地的記憶，後來都寫在《蠻書》與《新唐書·南蠻傳》之中，成為南詔記載裡最重的一筆。
resultEn: The result was that Nanzhao gained and Tang lost. After the city fell the garrison broke up, the commander died in the breach, and the Annan Protectorate of the Tang existed in name only; there was no longer a screen between Lingnan and Yunnan. Nanzhao could push its line down to the lower Red River, take the rice, the sea route and the customs, and keep troops in the fields outside the city while waiting for the next moment to strike. For more than a decade afterwards the tug-of-war between Tang and Nanzhao over Jiaozhi never resolved. The court sent commanders for Jiaozhi again and again in the Xiantong years, and the Ministry of War issued grain again and again, but because the troops were never full, the grain never came in time, and the commanders never coordinated with one another, opportunity was missed until Gao Pian, as protector of Annan, recovered Aizhou and Xuanzhou and pushed the Nanzhao offensive back north of the Red River. As for the battle itself, what can be settled is this: the elephants and the infantry of Nanzhao broke the Tang defences of Jiaozhi, and the city changed hands; the Tang crossbowmen held the attackers off the wall for a long while, and could not save it in the end. The memory of that lost province in the Tang is written into the Manshu and the Account of the Southern Barbarians, and it is the heaviest single entry in the Nanzhao record.
